capacity.interpretation: The POINT ESTIMATE (continuing forward exactly what this tape showed: zero qualifying pre-start episodes in 8.27 days across 79 candidate games) is $0/month, far below the $20 bar. The statistical UPPER BOUND scenario -- which asks how large the true rate could plausibly be and still be consistent with observing zero in a sample this size -- is NOT ruled out from clearing the bar. Both are reported because a single point estimate of zero, on a short window, understates the genuine uncertainty about the forward rate; neither one is the 'answer' on its own.

point_estimate_scenario.arithmetic: 0.0000 episodes/month (continued forward from the observed 0 episodes / 8.27 tape-days) x any per-path edge x $10.00 notional/path = $0.0000/month (zero episodes makes the edge multiplier moot)

upper_bound_statistical_scenario.arithmetic: 290.7787 games/month x 0.037211 (95% one-sided upper bound qualifying rate) = 10.8202 qualifying games/month x $0.5100/$1-path edge x $10.00 notional/path = $55.1828/month
upper_bound_statistical_scenario.description: NOT a point estimate. Uses the primary statistic's own one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson upper bound on the game-level qualifying rate (honest answer to 'how high could the true rate plausibly be given 0/79 observed'), applied to this tape's own observed games/month cadence, at the single most generous per-path net edge measured ANYWHERE on the tape (post-start max, since pre-start itself never measured a positive fee-net edge at all).
upper_bound_statistical_scenario.scenario_edge_source: max net_edge_usd (fee-net only) observed on ANY after_scheduled_start priced path in this tape -- reused here only because pre-start priced paths never printed a positive value to draw a scenario edge from.

extra.analytics_cross_check_verdict: The tape independently reproduces the SHAPE of the spec's cited evidence_snapshot (market_phase heavily skewed to after_scheduled_start; pre_scheduled_start exactly 0; single_snapshot_share ~0.73-0.75; persistent_cases_ge_2_snapshots in the low teens) even though this session's window (8.27 days, ending later) is neither the same window nor the cited 14 days -- 56 lifetime cases vs 55 cited, 0 vs 0 pre-start, 55 vs 53 post-start, 1 vs 2 unknown, 15 vs 14 persistent, 0.732 vs 0.745 single-snapshot share. Close enough on every dimension to say the two datasets describe the same underlying process on overlapping-but-not-identical windows; NOT close enough (nor intended) to be read as re-deriving the exact cited figures, and the spec's '14-day' label does not match this tape's actual ~8.3-day span -- reported plainly rather than parroted.

extra.recommendation: Not worth pursuing settlement-equivalence review on the strength of this evidence. The primary, pre-registered statistic is a clean, robust zero (0/79 games, 95% CI upper bound 4.56%, stable across every slippage/threshold/persistence stress cell), and the raw pre-start price data shows the two venues tracking each other almost exactly (fee-net edge never once positive across 72,875 priced pre-start paths) -- this is evidence of an efficient pregame relationship, not an under-sampled rare event. Independently, entry_logic precondition #4 (settlement_equivalence.state=='verified') is a hard, deterministic FAIL today (config/settlement_equivalence.yaml: decision='not_equivalent', approval=null) and nothing in this tape replay can move it -- that is a governance/documentation decision, not a data question, so more tape collection would not change this precondition's status. The one caveat: the statistical upper-bound scenario (games/month x 95% upper-bound qualifying rate x the single largest edge measured anywhere on the tape, borrowed from post-start since pre-start never had a positive value to draw from) reaches ~$55/month, above the $20 bar -- so a true rate this low CANNOT be fully excluded by 79 games of data alone. That caveat is reported honestly but should not be read as grounds for continued investment: it requires assuming both the loosest statistically-consistent rate AND a post-start-magnitude edge that has literally never been observed pre-start, simultaneously. On the evidence in hand, this is a no-go, and settlement-equivalence review would be spending real review effort on a strategy that -- even if the review cleared it -- has not shown an executable pre-start edge to trade.

performance.clv_note: No CLV concept applies to this strategy family. This is a cross-venue PARITY harvest (fair_value_model.type='cross_venue_parity'), not a probability-model edge measured against a sharp external closing line; the spec's own fair_value_model states the fair value for each leg IS the other venue's quote, so there is no independent close to mark CLV against. The key is present (schema-required) and honestly null, mirroring the same rationale strat_p022_fade_v2's validation used for a different reason (settlement mechanic, not price-disagreement).
performance.net_edge_units: USD per $1 notional path, fee-net only (no slippage), MEDIAN across the 72,875 priced pre_scheduled_start paths in this tape. Reported as a descriptive/diagnostic figure, NOT a per-trade P&L -- there were zero qualifying pre-start trades to average. p95 = -$0.04/path, max = -$0.01/path: the parity relationship held almost exactly pre-start and NEVER once printed a positive fee-net edge across the whole pre-start sample, before slippage or the $0.03 threshold are even applied.

stress_tests.summary: The pre-start qualifying count is ZERO at every single stress-test cell tried: all 4 slippage levels (0c/0.5c/1c/2c per leg), all 3 thresholds (2c/3c/5c), and both persistence requirements (>=1 snapshot / >=2 consecutive snapshots). This is not a fragile result sitting near a boundary -- it holds even at the loosest combination tested (threshold $0.02, zero slippage). The underlying raw fee-net edge distribution pre-start (max -$0.01 across 72,875 priced paths) confirms the zero is a property of the price data itself, not an artifact of any one filter choice in this replay.

uncertainty.method: Clopper-Pearson EXACT binomial CI on the GAME-level proportion (k games with >=1 pre-start qualifying persistent episode / n games with >=1 pre-start matched observation), i.e. clustered by game, not pooled by raw path/snapshot count (forbidden shortcut explicitly avoided per spec extra.validation_guidance). k=0, n=79. Point estimate 0.0%, 95% CI [0.0%, 4.56%], one-sided 95% upper bound 3.72% (rule-of-three approx 3/79=3.80%, consistent).
